issue_text: testFileSuffixes includes the exotic TS module variants .test.mts/.cts and .spec.mts/.cts but omits the common JS module variants .test.mjs/.cjs and .spec.mjs/.cjs. The list is documented as "conventional TS/JS test-file endings (shared across Jest and Vitest)" and is shared (via embedding) by vitestConvention. Vitest's own default include glob is `**/*.{test,spec}.?(c|m)[jt]s?(x)`, which DOES match `.test.mjs`, `.test.cjs`, `.spec.mjs`, `.spec.cjs`. So a Vitest repo with a `foo.test.mjs` (or `.cjs`) test file has IsTestFile return false for it: it is excluded from the reproduction partition, DirHasTests, and DeletesATest test-file detection.

In goConvention.DeletesATest the guard `if strings.HasPrefix(line, "---") { continue }` is dead. The only match performed on the line is testFuncRemovedRe = `^-func (Test|Benchmark|Fuzz|Example)...`, which requires the line to begin with `-func`. A line beginning with `---` cannot begin with `-func` (char 1 is `-`, not `f`), so no `---`-prefixed line could ever match the regex. Deleting the entire guard leaves behavior identical, and every existing test still passes.

typeScriptConvention.DeletesATest (and the identical pythonConvention.DeletesATest at python.go:177) classifies a hunk line with `case strings.HasPrefix(line, "---"), strings.HasPrefix(line, "+++")` as a file header BEFORE the `inHunk && inTestFile && strings.HasPrefix(line, "-")` removal case. A removed CONTENT line whose original text starts with `--` appears in the unified diff as `---<rest>` and is therefore swallowed by the header case, so it never triggers the deletion gate.
